solution: Equal arcs give equal chords, as in example-3: AD = BE because the arcs are equal.
Chords that do not cross inside the circle either do not meet at all (parallel) or meet outside the circle.

So these chords are not parallel, and equal arcs alone do not make the chords parallel.

answers.answer: An angle has exactly one bisector, so ∠BEC has one bisector.
solution: A bisector of an angle is the ray from its vertex that divides the angle into two equal angles.
Only one such ray exists, because it must make each part half of m(∠BEC).
So ∠BEC has exactly one bisector.
Answer: 1.

answers.answer: Yes, inscribed angles that include arcs of equal measure (in the same circle or congruent circles) are equal in measure.
solution: Each inscribed angle equals half the measure of the arc it includes.
If the two arcs have equal measures, their halves are equal.
So the two inscribed angles are equal in measure.

answers.answer: △ACE is isosceles because m(∠ACE) = m(∠CAE), so EA = EC.
solution: AB = CD, so m(arc AB) = m(arc CD).
Arc AB = arc AC + arc CB and arc CD = arc CA + arc AD.
Subtract arc AC from both sides: m(arc CB) = m(arc AD).
∠CAB includes arc CB and ∠ACD includes arc AD.
So m(∠CAE) = m(∠ACE).
In △ACE, equal angles mean EA = EC, so the triangle is isosceles (Q.E.D.).

answers.answer: m(∠AEB) = m(∠AEC), because they include equal arcs AB and AC.
solution: AB = AC, so m(arc AB) = m(arc AC).
∠AEB is inscribed and includes arc AB.
∠AEC is inscribed and includes arc AC.
Inscribed angles on equal arcs are equal.
So m(∠AEB) = m(∠AEC) (Q.E.D.).

answers.answer: Yes: ∠ABD and ∠ACD are equal and on the same base AD and the same side.
solution: DA = DC, so m(∠DCA) = m(∠DAC) = 25°.
So m(∠ACD) = m(∠ABD) = 25°, both drawn on base AD and on one side of it.
So A, B, C, D lie on one circle.

answers.answer: Yes: ∠DAC and ∠DBC are equal and on the same base DC and the same side.
solution: EA = ED, so m(∠EDA) = m(∠EAD).
EB = EC, so m(∠EBC) = m(∠ECB).
AD ∥ BC, so m(∠DAC) = m(∠ACB) and m(∠ADB) = m(∠DBC).
So m(∠DAC) = m(∠ACB) = m(∠EBC) = m(∠DBC).
So m(∠DAC) = m(∠DBC), both drawn on base DC and on one side of it.
So A, B, C, D lie on one circle.

answers.answer: Yes: ∠ADB and ∠ACB are equal and on the same base AB and the same side.
solution: In the rectangle, AD = BC, AB is common and m(∠DAB) = m(∠CBA) = 90°.
So △DAB and △CBA are congruent, so m(∠ADB) = m(∠ACB).
Both are drawn on base AB and on one side of it.
So A, B, C, D lie on one circle.

answers.answer: Yes: ∠ADB and ∠ACB are equal and on the same base AB and the same side.
solution: In the square, AD = BC, AB is common and m(∠DAB) = m(∠CBA) = 90°.
So △DAB and △CBA are congruent, so m(∠ADB) = m(∠ACB) = 45°.
Both are drawn on base AB and on one side of it.
So A, B, C, D lie on one circle.

answers.answer: No: in a general parallelogram the angles on one base are not equal.
solution: In a parallelogram AD ∥ BC but AD = BC with no right angles, so ∠ADB and ∠ACB are not equal in general.
There are no two equal angles drawn on one base and on one side of it.
So a circle does not pass through A, B, C, D.
